title: NULL keys group together and do not match in `=` joins; `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` matches them
verdict: NULLs group together; `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` joins them; no `<=>`
description: An equi-join on `=` does not match NULL keys; one on `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` does. A full join keeps each NULL row unmatched. `x IN (SELECT NULL)` and `x NOT IN (2, NULL)` are NULL. `GROUP BY` puts the NULLs in one group.
The spelling is `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`; MySQL's `<=>` is not a DuckDB operator (Binder Error).
reference: Grouping and `DISTINCT` put NULLs together; an equi-join's `=` does not match NULL, and keys compared with `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` do (reference-semantics.md, NULL).
